page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 vCPUs allocated across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 15.0 GB, yielding 1.88 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD disk capacity. Networking is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Built-in CPU flags include hardware support for AVX and AES instructions, though modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI are not present.

Benchmark data demonstrates moderate multi-threaded performance alongside weak single-core capacity. In multi-core tests, the c3.2xlarge achieved a stress-ng score of 6681.49 and a PassMark CPU rating of 7237.82, placing it in average benchmark tiers. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain low, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 717.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1280.58. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 50.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 37.77 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect average throughput for software compilation with Clang and static web serving at 6.84 GB/sec, while Redis operations and LLM text generation rank weak to poor.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the c3.2xlarge couples dedicated compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage within a single instance allocation. Tradeoffs center on legacy single-core efficiency and the absence of advanced vector instruction sets, which limits modern machine learning inference performance. The hardware configuration is best suited for multi-threaded build jobs, software compilation, static web server hosting, legacy batch processing, and lightweight database applications requiring direct-attached NVMe storage.
